title: US Leaders and Diaspora Mark India's 80th Independence Day With Parades and Proclamations
excerpt: Massachusetts declared August 15 as 'India Day,' while community celebrations from San Jose to New York honor the dual milestone of India at 80 and America at 250.
body:
• Massachusetts Governor Maura Healey and Boston Mayor Michelle Wu declared August 15 as "India Day," recognizing the Indian diaspora's contributions to the state.
  • Congressman Shri Thanedar introduced a resolution in the U.S. House to designate August 15 as the "National Day of Celebration of the World's Two Largest Democracies."
  • Major celebrations are planned across the country, including AIA SWADES 2026 in San Jose, the 15th India Day Parade in New York, and NAIO's Azadi Ka Mahotsav on Long Island.
  • This year's Independence Day carries added significance as it coincides with America's 250th anniversary, with both nations' diaspora communities celebrating shared democratic values.

As India marks its 80th Independence Day on August 15, 2026, American political leaders and Indian diaspora communities across the United States are observing the milestone with proclamations, parades, and large-scale cultural events — many of them framing the occasion around the parallel celebration of America's 250th anniversary.

Official Proclamations

Massachusetts Governor Maura Healey issued a proclamation on August 1 officially designating August 15 as "India Day," citing the vital role played by Indian-American community organizations in promoting civic engagement, cultural exchange, and mutual understanding. The proclamation noted that more than five million people of Indian descent live in the United States, contributing to social, economic, and civic life.

Boston Mayor Michelle Wu followed with a similar proclamation, welcoming the opening of a new Indian Consulate in Boston and celebrating the visit of INS Sudarshini during the SAILBOSTON-250 event.

In Washington, Indian-American Congressman Shri Thanedar introduced a resolution in the U.S. House of Representatives to declare August 15 as the "National Day of Celebration of the World's Two Largest Democracies." The resolution, co-sponsored by Congressmen Buddy Carter and Brad Sherman, noted that Americans of Indian heritage serve as government officials, military personnel, and law enforcement officers who "diligently uphold the principles of the US Constitution."

Celebrations Coast to Coast

In the Bay Area, the Association of Indo Americans (AIA) is hosting AIA SWADES 2026 at Plaza de Cesar Chavez in downtown San Jose on August 15. The event features Bollywood actress Taapsee Pannu as Grand Marshal, with Consul General of India Dr. Srikar Reddy and San Jose Mayor Matt Mahan among the distinguished guests. More than 50 floats and marching groups, cultural performances, an international food festival, and a fashion show are planned, with events running from 2 p.m. to 10 p.m.

"NAIO is committed to uniting Indian Americans across social, cultural, professional, business, and religious organizations to create a stronger, more influential, and collaborative community."

— Dr. Raj Bhayani, Founder Trustee, NAIO

On the East Coast, the 15th India Day Parade USA 2026 launched with a packed curtain raiser at the Theodore Roosevelt Executive & Legislative Building in Mineola, New York, drawing more than 250 attendees. The parade will commemorate the 80th anniversary with participation from New York State Senator Steven D. Rhoads, Town Supervisor Jennifer DeSena, and Consul General of India staff in New York.

The National Alliance of Indian Organizations (NAIO), in collaboration with the Consulate General of India in New York, hosted an Azadi Ka Mahotsav curtain raiser at the consulate on July 17, previewing its August 15 celebration at the Long Island Marriott in Uniondale. In Silicon Valley, Americans4Hindus and Festival of Globe are holding a week-long celebration from August 14-17 in Fremont, combining cultural heritage with civic engagement.

The Dual Milestone

Several organizers have framed this year's celebrations around the convergence of India's 80th Independence Day and America's semiquincentennial. The AIA SWADES event is titled "The U.S.'s 250th & India's 80th Independence Day Celebrations," while NAIO's programming explicitly bridges the two democracies' founding stories.

The shared framing is consistent with an ongoing Congressional push. The House resolution introduced by Thanedar references Prime Minister Narendra Modi's June state visit to the United States, which, the resolution states, "anchored the United States and India in a new level of trust and mutual understanding."

What's Next

Indian consulates across the United States will host flag-hoisting ceremonies on August 15. Community organizations are encouraging Indian Americans to attend local celebrations and engage in civic activities that strengthen the diaspora's collective voice. For NRIs and Indian Americans in the Bay Area, AIA SWADES in San Jose represents the largest local Independence Day gathering; those on the East Coast can join the India Day Parade and NAIO events across the New York metropolitan area.
